passages.text: Now there was a man named Elkanah who was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was a man.
He lived in Ramathaim-zophim.
This place was in the hill country of Ephraim.
Elkanah was an Ephraimite.
His father was Jeroham.
Jeroham’s father was Elihu.
Elihu’s father was Tohu.
Tohu’s father was Zuph.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֜ד מִן־ הָרָמָתַ֛יִם צוֹפִ֖ים מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וּשְׁמ֡וֹ אֶ֠לְקָנָה בֶּן־ יְרֹחָ֧ם בֶּן־ אֱלִיה֛וּא בֶּן־ תֹּ֥חוּ בֶן־ צ֖וּף אֶפְרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was a man from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim.
He had two wives.
One wife was named Hannah.
The other wife was named Peninnah.
Peninnah had children.
Hannah had no children.
passages.original: וְלוֹ֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשִׁ֔ים שֵׁ֤ם אַחַת֙ חַנָּ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית פְּנִנָּ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י לִפְנִנָּה֙ יְלָדִ֔ים וּלְחַנָּ֖ה אֵ֥ין יְלָדִֽים׃

passages.text: Year after year Elkanah would go up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was a man from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim.
He lived in his city with his family.
Every year, Elkanah left his city.
He went to Shiloh.
He went there to worship the LORD of Hosts.
He also went there to offer sacrifices to the LORD.
At Shiloh, Eli’s two sons served as priests.
Their names were Hophni and Phinehas.
They were priests to the LORD.
passages.original: וְעָלָה֩ הָאִ֨ישׁ הַה֤וּא מֵֽעִירוֹ֙ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀ יָמִ֔ימָה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֧ת וְלִזְבֹּ֛חַ לַיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בְּשִׁלֹ֑ה וְשָׁ֞ם שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־ עֵלִ֗י חָפְנִי֙ וּפִ֣נְחָ֔ס כֹּהֲנִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And whenever the day came for Elkanah to present his sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was a man with two wives.
One wife was named Peninnah.
Peninnah had sons and daughters.
On the day Elkanah offered his sacrifice, he gave portions of the sacrifice to Peninnah.
He also gave portions to all of Peninnah’s sons.
He gave portions to all of Peninnah’s daughters.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיִּזְבַּ֖ח אֶלְקָנָ֑ה וְנָתַ֞ן לִפְנִנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וּֽלְכָל־ בָּנֶ֛יהָ וּבְנוֹתֶ֖יהָ מָנֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved her even though the LORD had closed her womb.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was Hannah’s husband.
Elkanah gave Hannah a double portion.
Elkanah loved Hannah.
The LORD had closed Hannah’s womb.
passages.original: וּלְחַנָּ֕ה יִתֵּ֛ן מָנָ֥ה אַחַ֖ת אַפָּ֑יִם כִּ֤י אֶת־ חַנָּה֙ אָהֵ֔ב וַֽיהוָ֖ה סָגַ֥ר רַחְמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Because the LORD had closed Hannah’s womb, her rival would provoke her and taunt her viciously.
passages.sermon:
Hannah could not have children.
The LORD had closed Hannah’s womb.
Peninnah was Hannah’s rival.
Peninnah provoked Hannah.
Peninnah taunted Hannah cruelly.
Peninnah did this because Hannah had no children.
passages.original: וְכִֽעֲסַ֤תָּה צָֽרָתָהּ֙ גַּם־ כַּ֔עַס בַּעֲב֖וּר הַרְּעִמָ֑הּ כִּֽי־ סָגַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד רַחְמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And this went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival taunted her until she wept and would not eat.
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman who could not have children because the LORD had closed her womb.
Hannah had a rival who taunted her.
This happened every year.
Each time Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, her rival provoked her.
Hannah wept.
Hannah would not eat.
passages.original: וְכֵ֨ן יַעֲשֶׂ֜ה שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֗ה מִדֵּ֤י עֲלֹתָהּ֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה כֵּ֖ן תַּכְעִסֶ֑נָּה וַתִּבְכֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תֹאכַֽל׃

passages.text: “Hannah, why are you crying?” her husband Elkanah asked. “Why won’t you eat? Why is your heart so grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was Hannah’s husband.
He saw that Hannah was upset.
He spoke to her.
He said, “Hannah, why are you crying?”
He asked, “Why won’t you eat?”
He asked, “Why is your heart so sad?”
He said, “Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לָ֜הּ אֶלְקָנָ֣ה אִישָׁ֗הּ חַנָּה֙ לָ֣מֶה תִבְכִּ֗י וְלָ֙מֶה֙ לֹ֣א תֹֽאכְלִ֔י וְלָ֖מֶה יֵרַ֣ע לְבָבֵ֑ךְ הֲל֤וֹא אָֽנֹכִי֙ ט֣וֹב לָ֔ךְ מֵעֲשָׂרָ֖ה בָּנִֽים׃

passages.text: So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman who suffered because she could not have children.
She and her family went to Shiloh to worship the LORD.
After they finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up.
Eli was the priest of the LORD.
Eli sat on a chair.
The chair was by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
passages.original: וַתָּ֣קָם חַנָּ֔ה אַחֲרֵ֛י אָכְלָ֥ה בְשִׁלֹ֖ה וְאַחֲרֵ֣י שָׁתֹ֑ה וְעֵלִ֣י הַכֹּהֵ֗ן יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־ הַכִּסֵּ֔א עַל־ מְזוּזַ֖ת הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: In her bitter distress, Hannah prayed to the LORD and wept with many tears.
passages.sermon:
Hannah felt deep sorrow.
She was in bitter distress.
Hannah prayed to the LORD.
She wept with many tears.
passages.original: וְהִ֖יא מָ֣רַת נָ֑פֶשׁ וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל עַל־ יְהוָ֖ה וּבָכֹ֥ה תִבְכֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And she made a vow, pleading, “O LORD of Hosts, if only You will look upon the affliction of Your maidservant and remember me, not forgetting Your maidservant but giving her a son, then I will dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever come over his head.”
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman in deep distress.
She made a vow to the LORD of Hosts.
She spoke directly to God.
She said, “LORD of Hosts, please see my suffering.
I am Your servant.
Remember me.
Do not forget me.
Give me a son.
If You give me a son, I will give him to You.
He will belong to the LORD all his life.
No razor will touch his head.”
passages.original: וַתִּדֹּ֨ר נֶ֜דֶר וַתֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אִם־ רָאֹ֥ה תִרְאֶ֣ה׀ בָּעֳנִ֣י אֲמָתֶ֗ךָ וּזְכַרְתַּ֙נִי֙ וְלֹֽא־ תִשְׁכַּ֣ח אֶת־ אֲמָתֶ֔ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֥ה לַאֲמָתְךָ֖ זֶ֣רַע אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּנְתַתִּ֤יו לַֽיהוָה֙ כָּל־ יְמֵ֣י חַיָּ֔יו וּמוֹרָ֖ה לֹא־ יַעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: As Hannah kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman in deep distress.
She prayed for a long time before the LORD.
Eli was the priest at the temple.
Eli watched Hannah’s mouth as she prayed.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ כִּ֣י הִרְבְּתָ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְעֵלִ֖י שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֶת־ פִּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Hannah was praying in her heart, and though her lips were moving, her voice could not be heard. So Eli thought she was drunk and said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!”
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman who prayed to the LORD.
She prayed silently in her heart.
Her lips moved as she prayed.
No one could hear her voice.
Eli was the priest at the temple.
Eli saw Hannah.
Eli watched her lips move.
Eli did not hear her voice.
Eli thought Hannah was drunk.
Eli spoke to Hannah.
Eli said, “How long will you be drunk?”
Eli said, “Put away your wine.”
passages.original: וְחַנָּ֗ה הִ֚יא מְדַבֶּ֣רֶת עַל־ לִבָּ֔הּ רַ֚ק שְׂפָתֶ֣יהָ נָּע֔וֹת וְקוֹלָ֖הּ לֹ֣א יִשָּׁמֵ֑עַ וַיַּחְשְׁבֶ֥הָ עֵלִ֖י לְשִׁכֹּרָֽה׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ עֵלִ֔י עַד־ מָתַ֖י תִּשְׁתַּכָּרִ֑ין הָסִ֥ירִי אֶת־ יֵינֵ֖ךְ מֵעָלָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: “No, my lord,” Hannah replied. “I am a woman oppressed in spirit. I have not had any wine or strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Hannah spoke to Eli.
She said, “No, my lord.”
Hannah was a woman with a troubled spirit.
She had not drunk wine.
She had not drunk strong drink.
Hannah poured out her soul before the LORD.
passages.original: וַתַּ֨עַן חַנָּ֤ה וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֲדֹנִ֔י אִשָּׁ֤ה קְשַׁת־ ר֙וּחַ֙ אָנֹ֔כִי וְיַ֥יִן וְשֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי וָאֶשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; for all this time I have been praying out of the depth of my anguish and grief.”
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman who prayed to the LORD.
She spoke to Eli, the priest.
She said, “Do not think I am a wicked woman.
I am your servant.
I have not done evil.
I have been speaking because I am very troubled.
I have much sorrow and pain.
I have prayed for a long time because of my anguish and grief.”
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־ אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ לִפְנֵ֖י בַּת־ בְּלִיָּ֑עַל כִּֽי־ מֵרֹ֥ב שִׂיחִ֛י וְכַעְסִ֖י דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי עַד־ הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: “Go in peace,” Eli replied, “and may the God of Israel grant the petition you have asked of Him.”
passages.sermon:
Eli was the high priest of Israel.
Eli answered Hannah.
Eli said, “Go in peace.”
Eli said, “May the God of Israel give you what you have asked from Him.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַן עֵלִ֛י וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְכִ֣י לְשָׁל֑וֹם וֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל יִתֵּן֙ אֶת־ שֵׁ֣לָתֵ֔ךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתְּ מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “May your maidservant find favor with you,” said Hannah. Then she went on her way, and she began eating again, and her face was no longer downcast.
passages.sermon:
Hannah spoke to Eli.
She said, “May your servant find favor in your eyes.”
Hannah left and went on her way.
She began to eat again.
Her face was no longer sad.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר תִּמְצָ֧א שִׁפְחָתְךָ֛ חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ הָאִשָּׁ֤ה לְדַרְכָּהּ֙ וַתֹּאכַ֔ל וּפָנֶ֥יהָ לֹא־ הָיוּ־ לָ֖הּ עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: The next morning Elkanah and Hannah got up early to bow in worship before the LORD, and then returned home to Ramah. And Elkanah had relations with his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was Hannah’s husband.
Elkanah and Hannah got up early the next morning.
They bowed down and worshiped before the LORD.
Afterward, they returned to their home in Ramah.
Elkanah had relations with his wife Hannah.
The LORD remembered Hannah.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣מוּ בַבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲווּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֛בוּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־ בֵּיתָ֖ם הָרָמָ֑תָה וַיֵּ֤דַע אֶלְקָנָה֙ אֶת־ חַנָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיִּֽזְכְּרֶ֖הָ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So in the course of time, Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him from the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Hannah was a woman who prayed to the LORD for a child.
After some time, Hannah became pregnant.
Hannah gave birth to a son.
Hannah named her son Samuel.
Hannah said, “I asked the LORD for him.”
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ לִתְקֻפ֣וֹת הַיָּמִ֔ים וַתַּ֥הַר חַנָּ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א אֶת־ שְׁמוֹ֙ שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י מֵיְהוָ֖ה שְׁאִלְתִּֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Elkanah and all his house went up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow, but Hannah did not go. “After the boy is weaned,” she said to her husband, “I will take him to appear before the LORD and to stay there permanently.”
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was Hannah’s husband.
Elkanah lived with his family.
Elkanah went up with all his household.
He went to offer the yearly sacrifice to the LORD.
He went to fulfill his vow to the LORD.
Hannah did not go with them.
Hannah spoke to her husband.
She said, “I will not go until the boy is weaned.”
She said, “After I have weaned him, I will take him.”
She said, “I will bring him to appear before the LORD.”
She said, “He will stay there forever.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֛עַל הָאִ֥ישׁ אֶלְקָנָ֖ה וְכָל־ בֵּית֑וֹ לִזְבֹּ֧חַ לַֽיהוָ֛ה אֶת־ זֶ֥בַח הַיָּמִ֖ים וְאֶת־ נִדְרֽוֹ׃ וְחַנָּ֖ה לֹ֣א עָלָ֑תָה כִּֽי־ אָמְרָ֣ה לְאִישָׁ֗הּ עַ֣ד יִגָּמֵ֤ל הַנַּ֙עַר֙ וַהֲבִאֹתִ֗יו וְנִרְאָה֙ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וְיָ֥שַׁב שָׁ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: “Do what you think is best,” her husband Elkanah replied, “and stay here until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD confirm His word.” So Hannah stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
passages.sermon:
Elkanah was Hannah’s husband.
Elkanah spoke to Hannah.
He said, “Do what you think is best.”
He told her, “Stay here until you have weaned the boy.”
He said, “Only may the LORD confirm His word.”
Hannah stayed at home.
She nursed her son.
She nursed him until she had weaned him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהּ֩ אֶלְקָנָ֨ה אִישָׁ֜הּ עֲשִׂ֧י הַטּ֣וֹב בְּעֵינַ֗יִךְ שְׁבִי֙ עַד־ גָּמְלֵ֣ךְ אֹת֔וֹ אַ֛ךְ יָקֵ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ דְּבָר֑וֹ וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ וַתֵּ֣ינֶק אֶת־ בְּנָ֔הּ עַד־ גָּמְלָ֖הּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Once she had weaned him, Hannah took the boy with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. Though the boy was still young, she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
passages.sermon:
Hannah was the mother of the boy Samuel.
Hannah waited until she weaned her son Samuel.
After Samuel was weaned, Hannah took him with her.
Hannah brought a three-year-old bull.
Hannah brought an ephah of flour.
Hannah brought a skin of wine.
Samuel was still a young boy.
Hannah brought Samuel to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
passages.original: וַתַּעֲלֵ֨הוּ עִמָּ֜הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר גְּמָלַ֗תּוּ בְּפָרִ֤ים שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ וְאֵיפָ֨ה אַחַ֥ת קֶ֙מַח֙ וְנֵ֣בֶל יַ֔יִן וַתְּבִאֵ֥הוּ בֵית־ יְהוָ֖ה שִׁל֑וֹ וְהַנַּ֖עַר נָֽעַר׃

passages.text: And when they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.
passages.sermon:
Hannah was the mother of the boy.
Elkanah was her husband.
They had a young son.
They went to the house of the LORD at Shiloh.
They brought a bull with them.
They killed the bull.
They brought the boy to Eli.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ אֶת־ הַפָּ֑ר וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־ הַנַּ֖עַר אֶל־ עֵלִֽי׃

passages.text: “Please, my lord,” said Hannah, “as surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Hannah spoke to Eli.
She said, “Please, my lord.
As surely as you live, my lord, I speak to you now.
I am the woman who stood here with you before.
I stood here to pray to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י חֵ֥י נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֑י אֲנִ֣י הָאִשָּׁ֗ה הַנִּצֶּ֤בֶת עִמְּכָה֙ בָּזֶ֔ה לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: I prayed for this boy, and since the LORD has granted me what I asked of Him, I now dedicate the boy to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is dedicated to the LORD.” So they worshiped the LORD there.
passages.sermon:
Hannah is the mother of the boy Samuel.
Hannah prayed for this boy.
The LORD answered my prayer.
The LORD gave me what I asked for.
I give this boy to the LORD.
He belongs to the LORD all his life.
They worshiped the LORD there.
passages.original: אֶל־ הַנַּ֥עַר הַזֶּ֖ה הִתְפַּלָּ֑לְתִּי וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לִי֙ אֶת־ שְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖לְתִּי מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃ וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י הִשְׁאִלְתִּ֙הוּ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כָּל־ הַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֔ה ה֥וּא שָׁא֖וּל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ שָׁ֖ם לַיהוָֽה׃פ
